title: fix(cli): os migrate apply takes a database lock so concurrent migrators run one at a time
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9EtLz4Q3mytsuVUjBvqeWPK)_

Fixes #31598

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:`os migrate apply` 在真正读取待办表结构变更之前,先在主库上拿一把数据库级的会话锁(Postgres `pg_advisory_lock`、MySQL `GET_LOCK`,锁名固定为 `objectstack:schema-migrate`),命令结束时释放;SQLite 不加锁。
- **为什么改**:多副本部署时每个 Pod 的 init 容器都会跑一次迁移。实测 3 个迁移同时打同一个 Postgres:三个都报告"建了表"(82 + 86 + 37 张,库里实际 86 张),第三个还在别人建到一半的表上做了 drift 变更,而且全部退出码 0。
- **风险与回滚**:单机路径只多一条无竞争的加锁语句,输出逐字节不变(实测)。有竞争时多打印一行"正在等待",最多等 10 分钟,超时则拒绝、不做任何变更并以非零退出。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- **先看**:① `packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migration-lock.ts` 的 `acquireSchemaMigrationLock`;② `packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migrate.ts` 中 `bootSchemaStack` 里 `migrationLock` 的取锁点与 `shutdown()` 的释放;③ `schema-migration-lock.integration.test.ts`。
- **两分钟验证**:有本地 Postgres 时运行 `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL=postgres://… pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run src/utils/schema-migration-lock.integration.test.ts`,预期 4/4 通过:两个迁移排队等锁、只有一个建表、另一个报告 `in_sync`。
- **需要你做的**:无,席位落地

## The one exception to R3 this card accepts

R3 on #3814 (「同意：每张卡都只在"声明多副本并接上 Redis 驱动"时才生效」) keeps the single-node default path unchanged. This card names the one exception it accepts, in its item 2:

> 2. The lock is harmless on a single node (uncontended); keep its output identical apart from no new lines when uncontended. Note: this changes the single-node code path by one uncontended lock call; say so in the PR.

So, stated plainly: **on a single node, every applying `os migrate apply` now runs one extra statement** (`select pg_try_advisory_lock(…)` on Postgres, `select GET_LOCK(…, 0)` on MySQL) on a connection of its own, plus the matching unlock at the end. It is not gated behind declared replicas or a Redis driver, because the collision happens before any replica count is known to the migrator. Uncontended it prints nothing. Measured: one `os migrate apply --yes` on a fresh Postgres database, human face, gives byte-identical stdout and stderr on `origin/main` and on this diff over the same base once ISO timestamps and durations are normalized (stdout sha256 `8980fba0…1eda0`, 41,920 bytes, both sides; stderr empty, both sides). SQLite (and the Turso and WASM drivers on it) runs no statement at all.

## What changes

- **`packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migration-lock.ts` (new).** `acquireSchemaMigrationLock(driver, { database, warn, waitMs? })`. It reads the dialect from the driver's own knex client: `postgresql` takes `pg_advisory_lock`, `mysql` takes `GET_LOCK`, and every other dialect answers `null` and runs nothing. The flow is a no-wait try first (silent when it succeeds); on contention it prints ONE line naming the database and waits, bounded (Postgres `lock_timeout`, MySQL `GET_LOCK`'s seconds argument). If the wait runs out it throws a refusal naming the database, and the run migrates nothing. `release()` unlocks on the same session, then closes it. It is idempotent and never throws. Its own module, importing only `node:crypto`, so its pins load the lock and not the migration stack (`check:test-source-alias` asked for exactly that).
- **The key.** `SCHEMA_MIGRATION_LOCK_NAME = 'objectstack:schema-migrate'`, named once. The Postgres key is derived from it: the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 as a signed 64-bit integer, `255402229896085448`. The unit file pins the value, because a changed key would let an old and a new CLI migrate side by side during a rolling upgrade. It is not per-database: a Postgres advisory lock is already scoped to its database. MySQL's `GET_LOCK` is server-wide, see Acceptance notes.
- **The bound.** `SCHEMA_MIGRATION_LOCK_WAIT_MS = 10 * 60_000`, a constant. No environment override exists for migration timeouts, so none is added.
- **`packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migrate.ts`, `bootSchemaStack`.** A boot that can apply (a deferred boot that is not a read-only probe) takes the lock on the primary right after `runtime.start()`, before the coverage pass and before the first `previewDeferredSchemaWork()`. That boot held all its DDL back, so nothing has been written yet. A migrator that waited then reads only the work the first one left, which is none. `shutdown()` releases the lock first, in a `finally`. If one of the three post-lock reads (coverage, preview, package-table plan) throws, `underLock` releases it before the throw leaves. Which commands take it: `os migrate apply`, plus the `--apply` modes that boot deferred, `os migrate organization-ownership --apply` and `os migrate multi-value-columns --apply`. `os migrate plan` and every other read-only probe take none.
- **The session.** The lock rides a connection opened through the driver's own client (its configuration, credentials and TLS) but outside its pool, via knex `acquireRawConnection` / `destroyRawConnection`. See Acceptance note 1 for why not a pooled connection.
- **Changeset.** `@objectstack/cli` patch, with the claim's two lines at line start.

## Tests

- `packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migration-lock.test.ts` (new, unit, 16 cases, fake knex recording every statement and the session it ran on). The key value is pinned. SQLite / MSSQL / Oracle / no dialect / no knex answer `null` with no connection opened and no line. Postgres and MySQL each cover: uncontended, one statement and no line; release on the same session, once; contended, exactly one line naming the database, then the bounded wait (`lock_timeout` in ms, `GET_LOCK` in whole seconds); a wait that runs out refuses and closes the session. MySQL `GET_LOCK` answering `0` or `NULL` refuses. Any other wait failure is handed on unchanged.
- `packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migration-lock.integration.test.ts` (new, integration tier, live Postgres via `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL`, named skip without it). The contention is staged, not raced. The test holds the lock on its own session, spawns two `os migrate apply --yes --json` (`bin/run-dev.js`), waits until `pg_locks` shows both queued (an advisory lock not granted), then releases. Assertions: both queued (2); both exit 0 and each printed the wait line exactly once, on stderr, with stdout still one JSON document; exactly one created the schema and the other answered `in_sync` with nothing created; the table exists. A third, uncontended run is the control: no wait line, `in_sync`.
- No forced test edits.

## Acceptance notes

1. **Seat ruling 1 said "on the SAME connection the migration uses (a pooled second connection would not serialize)".** Measured otherwise, and taken by its intent. Both locks are session-scoped and exclude every other session on the database, the migration's own pooled ones included. The integration pin shows a lock held on a session outside both migrators' pools serializing them. What a pool breaks is the release: knex's pool gives no promise that the unlock runs on the session that locked, its idle reaper can close a held connection (silently releasing the lock), and an `OS_DATABASE_POOL_MAX=1` pool would have no connection left for the migration itself, so it would deadlock until the acquire timeout. So the lock takes its own session through the driver's own client and configuration. The seat may re-rule.
2. **Where the init container's command comes from.** `helm/` lives in the cloud repository, which this session cannot read. The card names `schema-migrate.ts`, whose `bootSchemaStack` is the `os migrate apply` path, so that is what is locked. If the chart's init container runs a SERVING boot with `OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT=1` (`os serve`, `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`) instead, its boot-time schema sync does not go through `bootSchemaStack` and this lock does not cover it. The same holds for any replica's own serving boot, whose additive sync runs at start. carrier: the cloud C2 card (the Helm hook Job), which decides which command the Job runs; noted, not filed.
3. **The non-deferred `--apply` data commands** (`os migrate meta --stored --apply`, `value-shapes --apply` and the others that boot plain) run their schema sync inside `runtime.start()`, before any point a lock could be taken without adding a kernel plugin. A plugin would add three INFO lines to every boot and break the byte-identical control. They are not locked. They are data repairs, not the schema migration this card names.
4. **MySQL.** `GET_LOCK` is server-wide, not per-database: two migrations of different databases on one MySQL server now run one after the other. That is harmless, only slower, and the seat ruled out per-database-name keys. NOT MEASURED live: the container has no MySQL server. The statements and result shapes are pinned in the unit file against mysql2's `[rows, fields]` shape.
5. **MSSQL / Oracle are out of scope, measured.** The CLI's primary database never is one: `resolveStandaloneDatabase` refuses their URL schemes ("Supported schemes: postgres://, pg://, mysql://, mysql2://, mongodb://, mongodb+srv://, libsql://, file:"). A declared datasource can be MSSQL, but the lock lives on the primary, which every migrator of the deployment shares.
6. **The refusal carries no error code.** It is a plain `Error` whose message names the database and the remedy, and `os migrate apply` prints it and exits 1 the way it handles any boot failure. A new ADR-0112 code would be a new public name, so it is listed as an open question for the seat rather than coined.

## Verification

Head `53aea71cf3cae9820396e0642854ee88cf3694db`, a clean merge with `origin/main` at `b126c1306`. Every reading below the ablations is on that head.
